Job Description
Master Explosive Ordnance Disposal Technicians are responsible for eliminating explosive and unconventional hazards which jeopardize operations
conducted in support of the National military strategy; manage and administer certification and Quality Assurance (QA) programs on Explosive Ordnance
Disposal (EOD) and diving systems and equipment to include Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation (RDT&E); responsible for training and
readiness assessments of the EOD and diving forces; plan, manage, and supervise all aspects of EOD operations; integrate EOD forces with joint/foreign
military and other local/state/federal agencies; assess manpower and resource requirements; and conduct long-range mission planning in support of EOD
operations.

common_text: Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Technicians locate, identify, render safe, defeat, exploit and dispose of foreign and domestic unexploded ordnance including conventional, chemical, biological, nuclear, underwater, and improvised devices, enabling access during military operations in support of Carrier and Expeditionary Strike Groups, Mine Countermeasures, Naval Special Warfare, and Army Special Forces; provide training and assistance for military, federal, state, and local civilian law enforcement agencies in Anti-terrorism/Force Protection procedures; support and conduct ordnance-related intelligence collection and counter-terrorism operations; operate, maintain, and repair specialized EOD and combat equipment; and maintain required forms, records, correspondence; and perform and supervise open and closed-circuit diving, explosive demolition, parachuting, small arms proficiency, and tactical delivery and extraction by unconventional insertion methods. __________________________________________

body:
Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Technicians locate, identify, render safe, defeat, exploit and dispose of foreign and domestic unexploded ordnance including conventional, chemical, biological, nuclear, underwater, and improvised devices, enabling access during military operations in support of Carrier and Expeditionary Strike Groups, Mine Countermeasures, Naval Special Warfare, and Army Special Forces; provide training and assistance for military, federal, state, and local civilian law enforcement agencies in Anti-terrorism/Force Protection procedures; support and conduct ordnance-related intelligence collection and counter-terrorism operations; operate, maintain, and repair specialized EOD and combat equipment; and maintain required forms, records, correspondence; and perform and supervise open and closed-circuit diving, explosive demolition, parachuting, small arms proficiency, and tactical delivery and extraction by unconventional insertion methods. __________________________________________

Master Explosive Ordnance Disposal Technicians are responsible for eliminating explosive and unconventional hazards which jeopardize operations conducted in support of the National military strategy; manage and administer certification and Quality Assurance (QA) programs on Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) and diving systems and equipment to include Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation (RDT&E); responsible for training and readiness assessments of the EOD and diving forces; plan, manage, and supervise all aspects of EOD operations; integrate EOD forces with joint/foreign military and other local/state/federal agencies; assess manpower and resource requirements; and conduct long-range mission planning in support of EOD operations.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
